name: showreel-22-squash

voice.text: Why do your photos look squashed? By default, your image fills its box exactly. When the box changes shape, the picture stretches with it. The fix: object fit, cover. It fills the box and crops the edges, so nothing stretches.

caption: Why do your photos look squashed? 📸 An is object-fit: fill by default: it fills its box exactly, so when the box has a different shape from the photo (a wide banner, a tall card on a phone), the picture is stretched to match. Add object-fit: cover and the image keeps its own shape: it still fills the whole box, and the edges that don't fit are cropped instead. Pick which part stays in view with object-position (center by default). Works in every major browser. Save it for your next card grid, or send it to whoever builds your site.

sources.note: MDN object-fit: fill is the initial value; the image fills the content box and is stretched when its aspect ratio differs; cover keeps the aspect ratio while filling the box and clips what doesn't fit
object-fit: Chrome 32, Edge 79, Firefox 36, Safari 10 (iOS mirrors)

tip.title: Why do your photos look squashed?
tip.why: An is object-fit: fill by default (MDN: the initial value), so it fills its box exactly and is stretched whenever the box has a different shape from the photo. object-fit: cover keeps the photo's own ratio, still fills the box, and crops the edges that don't fit; object-position picks which part stays in view.
